mathematical_checks.chain_aggregation: Each of the25 adjacent segments contributes to its original chain mean. Eight equally weighted chain means are the uncertainty units. Paired observed-minus-reconstructed differences retain within-chain covariance; nominal Student-t df7 intervals and pointwise bands do not assume200 segments or time origins are independent.
mathematical_checks.finite_origins_and_stationarity: The ensemble formula assumes stationary velocity correlations, while finite trajectories use lag-dependent origin sets. Their empirical MSD and VACF can therefore show residuals from finite origins/noise/nonstationarity/cadence even when the continuum identity is correct. Small residuals do not prove equilibration or rate/diffusion convergence.
mathematical_checks.fit_window_interpretation: A constant positive long-time MSD intercept lowers the logarithmic MSD slope below1 but alone leaves the unweighted linear slope unchanged. Window-dependent linear diffusivity requires curvature/transient running integral or finite-sample effects; the existing constant-intercept test correctly enforces this distinction.
mathematical_checks.numerical_quadrature_scope: Exactness is for the piecewise-linear interpolant of the saved VACF, not for unrecorded sub-cadence velocity motion. The separately retained double-trapezoid result is a numerical diagnostic and does not choose the physical model.
mathematical_checks.piecewise_linear_exactness: On interval i of width h with I_i=integral_0^ti C, integral_i I(t)dt=h*I_i+h^2*(2*C_i+C_(i+1))/6. This is the implemented increment, then multiplied by2. Constant C gives C*t^2; linear C0+a*t gives C0*t^2+a*t^3/3, including a nonuniform lag grid.
mathematical_checks.stationary_trace_identity: For the full three-dimensional velocity-dot correlation C(t), MSD(t)=2*integral_0^t (t-tau)*C(tau) dtau. The running Green-Kubo diffusivity is integral_0^t C(tau)dtau/3; the linear MSD slope is divided by6. No additional factor3 belongs in the trace MSD identity.
mathematical_checks.units: Lag inps times VACF inangstrom^2/ps^2 yields the correct angstrom^2/ps running diffusion after division by3 and angstrom^2 displacement after the second integral. The source uses molecular-COM displacement/velocity curves from the same frozen analysis.
